# Organs of the human body — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/human-organs.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/human-organs.ttl`](../decks/human-organs.ttl) · **Cards:** 44 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

44 organs and organ parts of the human body, from the brain to the lymph nodes. Front: the organ's common name in English and Swedish; back: its Latin name in Terminologia Anatomica (TA98). A note on the back names the organ system or the organ's main function. Compiled from Wikidata and Svensk MeSH (Karolinska Institutet's Swedish translation of MeSH), with the Latin checked against TA98 and the facts against the Swedish and English Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0-1.0. Its content comes from two open sources: Wikidata (CC0: labels, aliases and TA98 IDs) and Svensk MeSH (CC0, Karolinska Institutets Universitetsbibliotek: Swedish names and Swedish scope notes; NLM's English MeSH data in the same download, a U.S. Government work that NLM provides freely with acknowledgement, identified concepts and confirmed facts, and NLM's English scope notes informed the wording of several English back notes: brainstem, skin, nose, tongue, lungs, liver, lymph-node). Terminologia Anatomica (all rights reserved) sets the naming convention of the backs: each Latin back is the TA98 preferred term for the organ's code. That is a single standardised name, a fact rather than protected expression; for 33 cards the same term is also a Wikidata la label or alias, for several others it is in another open source or in the English Wikipedia (Membrana tympanica, in the Eardrum infobox), and three rest on TA98 alone (see Method). No definitions, descriptions, lists or selections were taken from TA98; the organ systems named in the notes are facts read from its hierarchy. The selection of organs is the compiler's own. The Swedish and English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used to verify names and the facts in the back notes; no selection was taken from them, and a few short factual phrases in the back notes follow their wording (for example retina, testis and large-intestine in Swedish). The back notes state short facts in plain wording written for the deck; where a phrase is close to a Svensk MeSH Swedish scope note ("Hörsel- och balansorgan", "syresätta blodet") that source is CC0 and cited, where it is close to an NLM English scope note that source is a U.S. Government work NLM provides freely, acknowledged here, and where it is close to a Wikipedia sentence it is a minimal factual statement, not protected expression; the notes that followed a Wikipedia sentence most closely (larynx, thymus, spinal-cord) were reworded in round 3. Attribution, though not required by CC0, is given in the deck (prov:wasDerivedFrom) and in this report: Karolinska Institutets Bibliotek for the Swedish MeSH translation and the U.S. National Library of Medicine for MeSH, as the Svensk MeSH page and NLM's terms ask, without implying NLM's endorsement.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Data and scripts. Every value below was fetched on 2026-10-04; the exact queries and the scripts run on the downloads are listed under Queries: search.py (wbsearchentities), mesh.py (Svensk MeSH tables), ta98.py (the TA98 entity-page parser) and gen.py (the evidence and check generator). gen.py read one further file, cards_spec.py, the compiler's per-card specification: the card texts, the Wikidata items, the TA98 code, the MeSH descriptor and the quotes to look up in the saved pages, all of which appear in the cards themselves. The raw responses and the scripts were kept only in the authoring session's temporary working directory and are not preserved; rerunning the listed queries and scripts reproduces the data, though the live sources may have changed since. The corrections made after the review rounds (Quality control, rounds 1 to 3) were made directly in this dossier, with the newly fetched pages listed under Queries.
3. Candidate list. The deck follows the human-skeleton deck's conventions. Candidates were the main organs of each organ system and a few well-known organ parts (of the eye, ear, larynx and intestine), about 80 in all, written down by the compiler without taking a list from any source. A SPARQL query looked up the Wikidata item of each candidate by English label, requiring a Terminologia Anatomica 98 ID (P1323); items it missed (the general heart and skin items, which have no P1323, and the brainstem, labelled "brain stem") were found with wbsearchentities. Where the general item has no P1323 the human-specific item that has it was used for the TA98 code (Q2419844 human heart, Q5259911 human skin). wbgetentities then fetched every candidate item's en, sv and la labels and aliases and its P1323 statements.
4. Latin names (back). For each candidate the TA98 entity page for its P1323 code was fetched from the TA98 online edition (ifaa.unifr.ch) and parsed for the Latin preferred term, Latin official synonym, English equivalent, English synonym and the TA98 hierarchy above the entry. The card's Latin text is the TA98 Latin preferred term for the item's code, so TA98 decides between Latin forms where several exist (Splen rather than Lien, Hypophysis rather than Glandula pituitaria, Nodus lymphoideus rather than Nodus lymphaticus, Vesica biliaris rather than Vesica fellea). A single standardised anatomical term is a fact, not protected expression, so TA98 (all rights reserved) is a verification source; no definitions, lists or other text were taken from it. TA98 prints the terms in lower case online; the cards capitalise the first letter, as the human-skeleton deck does. The same term is a Wikidata la label or alias for 33 of the 44 cards; for the others it was confirmed where possible in another open source (Encephalon an NLM MeSH entry term, Cornea and Hepar Wikidata en label or alias) or in the Swedish Wikipedia (verification: truncus encephali, vesica urinaria; it names gaster and splen too, but as the Greek names). Membrana tympanica is also the first Latin term in the English Wikipedia Eardrum article's infobox ("membrana tympanica; myringa"). Pulmones, Glandula thyroidea and Nodus lymphoideus are in no other source consulted and rest on TA98 alone. Every disagreement is listed under Quality control, round 0.
5. English names (front). The front gives the organ's common English name: an everyday English word where the English anatomical name equals the Latin and an everyday word exists (windpipe, voice box, womb, testicle); otherwise the usual English name, which is often the anatomical one (cerebellum, cornea, duodenum, pancreas). English spelling is British, as in the TA98 English equivalents (oesophagus, caecum). Each English name is a Wikidata en label or alias (checked) except "Windpipe" and the singular "Vocal fold", and each was cross-checked against the TA98 English equivalent or synonym, an NLM MeSH heading or entry term, or the English Wikipedia introduction.
6. Swedish names (front). The Swedish name is the Wikidata sv label or alias when it agrees with the Svensk MeSH 2026 term or synonym (Karolinska Institutets Universitetsbibliotek, CC0), compared case-insensitively; this holds for 38 cards. For binjure the Wikidata sv label is the singular of the Svensk MeSH plural term Binjurar; for lymfknuta it is the singular of the Svensk MeSH Swedish synonym Lymfknutor (main term Lymfkörtlar), and the Swedish note on that card names lymfkörtel as the other common name. Where the two disagree or one is missing, the open source with the common noun was followed and the name confirmed in the Swedish Wikipedia: öronspottkörtel, blindtarmsbihang and urinledare (Svensk MeSH terms; Wikidata has a Latin label, a definite form or nothing), and lungor (the plural of both sources' "lunga", since TA98 names the pair). Swedish names are written in lower case as common nouns and in the indefinite singular, as in the human-skeleton deck.
7. Back notes. A short note on each card names the organ system (from the TA98 hierarchy: nervous, respiratory, cardiovascular, digestive, urinary, reproductive, endocrine, lymphatic; organa sensuum as the sense organs) or, for an organ part, the organ it belongs to, and the organ's main function, in plain wording written for the deck. Swedish system names follow the Swedish Wikipedia article titles and redirects (nervsystemet, andningssystemet, hjärt- och kärlsystemet, matsmältningssystemet, urinsystemet, endokrina systemet, lymfsystemet; kvinnliga and manliga könsorganen). Some English notes follow the wording of NLM's English scope notes (brainstem, skin, nose, tongue, lungs, liver, lymph-node), a U.S. Government work that NLM provides freely; see Licensing. Each fact in a note was checked against a Svensk MeSH scope note (KIB's Swedish, or NLM's English one in the same download) where one states it, and against the Swedish or English Wikipedia; the supporting sentence is quoted in the card's evidence.
8. Cross-check. A script (gen.py, in the authoring session's temporary working directory) built each card's evidence from the saved raw data only: the Wikidata labels and P1323 values, the TA98 fields, the Svensk MeSH terms, synonyms, scope notes and entry terms, and the Wikipedia quotes, asserting that each quoted text occurs in the saved page or table (whitespace normalised) and that each Latin back equals the TA98 preferred term apart from capitalisation. For each card it added Wikidata checks for the P1323 code and for every en, sv and la label or alias that equals the card's text apart from capitalisation, using Wikidata's own spelling; every side with no such label was logged as a finding in round 0 with how it was resolved. The builder re-runs all checks against live Wikidata.
9. Uniqueness. Every front is unique in English and in Swedish and every Latin back is unique, so the deck is studied in both directions.

## Selection

44 cards: the brain, cerebellum, brainstem and spinal cord; the eye with the cornea and retina; the ear with the eardrum; the nose; the tongue; the skin; the heart; the lungs, windpipe, voice box and vocal fold; the parotid gland, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, duodenum, large intestine, caecum, appendix, rectum, liver, gallbladder and pancreas; the kidney, ureter and urinary bladder; the ovary, fallopian tube, uterus and testicle; the thyroid, adrenal, pituitary and pineal glands; and the spleen, thymus, palatine tonsil and lymph node. On the front, an everyday English word is used where the English anatomical name equals the Latin and an everyday word exists (windpipe, voice box, womb, testicle). An organ was included only if it has a TA98 code, a TA98 Latin preferred term that is unique in the deck, and an English and a Swedish name confirmed in two sources. Left out: the cerebrum, because TA98 makes cerebrum a synonym of telencephalon while the Swedish "storhjärna" is defined differently between sources; the colon, because Swedish uses tjocktarm and grovtarm for both the colon and the large intestine (Svensk MeSH and the Swedish Wikipedia disagree); the urethra, which TA98 splits into male and female entries; the jejunum, ileum, pharynx, epiglottis, iris, lens, cochlea, epididymis, prostate and vagina, left out only to keep the deck to about 40 cards (for all but the prostate, TA98 Latin prostata, the English name equals the TA98 Latin); the eyeball (no Swedish label in Wikidata or term in Svensk MeSH); the bronchi (Svensk MeSH's Swedish "luftrör" is also an everyday word for the windpipe); and vessels, muscles and tissues (aorta, diaphragm, pericardium, bone marrow), which are outside the deck's idea of organs. Bones are in the separate human-skeleton deck.

## Queries

**Find the Wikidata items of candidate organs by English label, with their TA98 ID (P1323) and en/sv/la labels and aliases (SPARQL at https://query.wikidata.org/sparql; saved as <scratch>/q1.rq, run with curl --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?item ?en (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?ta0;separator=" | ") AS ?ta) (SAMPLE(?sv0) AS ?sv) (SAMPLE(?la0) AS ?la) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?a;separator=" | ") AS ?enAliases) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?b;separator=" | ") AS ?svAliases) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?c;separator=" | ") AS ?laAliases) WHERE {
  VALUES ?en { "brain"@en "human brain"@en "cerebrum"@en "cerebellum"@en "brainstem"@en "spinal cord"@en "eye"@en "human eye"@en "eyeball"@en "cornea"@en "retina"@en "lens"@en "eardrum"@en "tympanic membrane"@en "ear"@en "nose"@en "human nose"@en "tongue"@en "human tongue"@en "skin"@en "human skin"@en "heart"@en "human heart"@en "lung"@en "human lung"@en "trachea"@en "larynx"@en "pharynx"@en "epiglottis"@en "vocal folds"@en "vocal cords"@en "vocal fold"@en "parotid gland"@en "esophagus"@en "human esophagus"@en "stomach"@en "human stomach"@en "small intestine"@en "duodenum"@en "jejunum"@en "ileum"@en "large intestine"@en "colon"@en "cecum"@en "appendix"@en "vermiform appendix"@en "rectum"@en "anus"@en "liver"@en "human liver"@en "gallbladder"@en "pancreas"@en "human pancreas"@en "kidney"@en "human kidney"@en "ureter"@en "urinary bladder"@en "urethra"@en "ovary"@en "human ovary"@en "uterus"@en "human uterus"@en "fallopian tube"@en "uterine tube"@en "testicle"@en "testis"@en "human testis"@en "prostate"@en "epididymis"@en "thyroid"@en "thyroid gland"@en "adrenal gland"@en "pituitary gland"@en "pineal gland"@en "spleen"@en "human spleen"@en "thymus"@en "palatine tonsil"@en "tonsil"@en "lymph node"@en "diaphragm"@en "thoracic diaphragm"@en "mammary gland"@en "breast"@en "penis"@en "vagina"@en "human vagina"@en "cochlea"@en "iris"@en "submandibular gland"@en "sublingual gland"@en "hypothalamus"@en "bone marrow"@en "aorta"@en "pericardium"@en "uvula"@en "palatine uvula"@en "gingiva"@en "scrotum"@en "cerebral cortex"@en "medulla oblongata"@en "pons"@en "thalamus"@en "olfactory bulb"@en "lacrimal gland"@en "sweat gland"@en "parathyroid gland"@en "bronchus"@en "main bronchus"@en }
  ?item rdfs:label ?en ; wdt:P1323 ?ta0 .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv0 FILTER(LANG(?sv0)="sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?la0 FILTER(LANG(?la0)="la") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?a FILTER(LANG(?a)="en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?b FILTER(LANG(?b)="sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?c FILTER(LANG(?c)="la") }
} GROUP BY ?item ?en
```

search.py (run as python3 <scratch>/search.py heart skin brainstem "human stomach" "human liver" "human kidney" "human spleen" eyeball):
import json, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request, os
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
out = {}
for s in sys.argv[1:]:
    url = "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&format=json&language=en&limit=6&search=" + urllib.parse.quote_plus(s)
    print(url)
    data = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})))
    out[s] = data
    for x in data["search"]:
        print("  ", x["id"], x.get("label"), "|", x.get("description"))
with open(os.path.join(D, "search-" + "_".join(a.replace(" ", "-") for a in sys.argv[1:])[:60] + ".json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(out, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
```

import json, os, re, sys, time, urllib.request, html
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.makedirs(os.path.join(D, "ta98"), exist_ok=True)
URL = "https://ifaa.unifr.ch/Public/EntryPage/TA98%20Tree/Entity%20TA98%20EN/{code}%20Entity%20TA98%20EN.htm"
codes = sys.argv[1:]
res = json.load(open(os.path.join(D, "ta98.json"))) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(D, "ta98.json")) else {}
for code in codes:
    c = code[1:] if code.startswith("A") else code
    path = os.path.join(D, "ta98", c + ".htm")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        url = URL.format(code=c)
        try:
            raw = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})).read()
        except Exception as e:
            print(code, "ERROR", e); continue
        open(path, "wb").write(raw)
        time.sleep(0.5)
    raw = open(path, "rb").read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    text = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]*>", "\n", raw))
    lines = [l.strip() for l in text.split("\n") if l.strip()]
    rec = {}
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if l in ("TA98 Latin preferred term", "TA98 Latin official synonym", "TA98 English equivalent", "TA98 English synonym", "TA98 Latin synonym") :
            rec.setdefault(l, []).append(lines[i + 1])
    try:
        h = lines.index("TA98 Hierarchy"); f = lines.index("FMA Taxonomy") if "FMA Taxonomy" in lines else len(lines)
        rec["hierarchy"] = lines[h + 1:f]
    except ValueError:
        pass
    rec["footer"] = [l for l in lines if "All rights reserved" in l]
    res[code] = rec
    print(code, {k: v for k, v in rec.items() if k != "footer"})
json.dump(res, open(os.path.join(D, "ta98.json"), "w"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
```

import csv, os, collections, sys, json
D = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "svmesh", "2026")
def rows(f):
    with open(os.path.join(D, f), encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:

terms = {r[0]: (r[1], r[2]) for r in rows("terms.csv") if len(r) >= 3}
byen = {v[0].lower(): k for k, v in terms.items()}
syn = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows("synonyms.csv"):
    if len(r) >= 2: syn[r[1]].append(r[0])

en = {r[1]: r[3] for r in rows("scope_notes.csv") if len(r) >= 4}
et = collections.defaultdict(list)

out = {}
for a in sys.argv[1:]:
    ui = a if a.startswith("D0") else byen.get(a.lower())
    if not ui:
        print(a, "NOT FOUND"); continue
    e, s = terms[ui]
    out[ui] = {"en": e, "sv": s, "syn": syn[ui], "sw_scope": sw.get(ui), "en_scope": en.get(ui), "entry": et[ui]}
    print(f"{ui} {e} | SV: {s} | syn: {'; '.join(syn[ui])}\n   SVSN: {sw.get(ui)}\n   ENSN: {en.get(ui)}\n   ET: {'; '.join(et[ui])[:300]}")
json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(D), "..", "mesh-out.json"), "w"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

**Build each card's evidence and Wikidata checks from the saved downloads (gen.py, run as python3 <scratch>/gen.py; reads <scratch>/entities.json, <scratch>/ta98.json, <scratch>/svmesh/2026/, the saved Wikipedia extracts and <scratch>/cards_spec.py; asserts every quote is in its saved page and every Latin back equals the TA98 preferred term; writes <scratch>/cards.json)** (Wikidata)

```
import csv, collections, json, os, re, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from cards_spec import SPEC
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
R = "2026-10-04"
ents = json.load(open(os.path.join(D, "entities.json")))
ta = json.load(open(os.path.join(D, "ta98.json")))
M = os.path.join(D, "svmesh", "2026")
def rows(f):
    with open(os.path.join(M, f), encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        return list(csv.reader(fh, delimiter="\t"))[1:]
terms = {r[0]: (r[1], r[2]) for r in rows("terms.csv") if len(r) >= 3}
syn = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows("synonyms.csv"):
    if len(r) >= 2: syn[r[1]].append(r[0])
msv = {r[0]: r[2] for r in rows("swe_scope_notes.csv") if len(r) >= 3}
men = {r[1]: r[3] for r in rows("scope_notes.csv") if len(r) >= 4}
met = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows("entryterms.csv"):
    if len(r) >= 2: met[r[0]].append(r[1])
wiki = {"sv": {}, "en": {}, "svf": {}}
for f in ("svwiki.json", "svwiki2.json"):
    wiki["sv"].update(json.load(open(os.path.join(D, f))))
wiki["en"].update(json.load(open(os.path.join(D, "enwiki.json"))))
for f in ("svwiki-full.json", "svwiki-ora.json"):
    for k, v in json.load(open(os.path.join(D, f))).items():
        if v["text"]:
            wiki["svf"][k] = v
ws = lambda s: re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()

def labels(q):
    e = ents[q]
    lab = {l: e.get("labels", {}).get(l, {}).get("value") for l in ("en", "sv", "la")}
    al = {l: [a["value"] for a in e.get("aliases", {}).get(l, [])] for l in ("en", "sv", "la")}
    return lab, al

def p1323(q):
    return [c["mainsnak"]["datavalue"]["value"] for c in ents[q].get("claims", {}).get("P1323", [])]

SYSTEMS = {}
cards, auto = [], []
nchecks = 0
for s in SPEC:
    text = {"en": s["en"], "sv": s["sv"], "la": s["la"]}
    items = [s["ta_item"]] + s["items"]
    checks = [{"qid": s["ta_item"], "property": "P1323", "expect": s["ta"]}]
    assert s["ta"] in p1323(s["ta_item"]), (s["id"], p1323(s["ta_item"]))
    evidence = []
    matched = {"en": False, "sv": False, "la": False}
    for q in items:
        lab, al = labels(q)
        parts = []
        for l in ("en", "sv", "la"):
            cands = ([lab[l]] if lab[l] else []) + al[l]
            hits = [c for c in cands if c.casefold() == text[l].casefold()]
            for h in hits:
                checks.append({"qid": q, "label": l, "equals": h})
                matched[l] = True
            desc = f"{l} label \"{lab[l]}\"" if lab[l] else f"no {l} label"
            extra = [a for a in hits if a != lab[l]]
            if extra:
                desc += "; " + l + " alias" + ("es " if len(extra) > 1 else " ") + ", ".join(f"\"{a}\"" for a in extra)
            parts.append(desc)
        codes = p1323(q)
        if codes:
            parts.append("P1323 (Terminologia Anatomica 98 ID) " + ", ".join(codes))
        else:
            parts.append("no P1323 statement")
        evidence.append({"source": "wikidata", "locator": f"https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/{q}", "says": "; ".join(parts), "retrieved": R})
    t = ta[s["ta"]]
    pref = t["TA98 Latin preferred term"][0]
    assert pref.casefold() == s["la"].casefold(), (s["id"], pref)
    h = t["hierarchy"]
    system = h[3] if len(h) > 3 else "?"
    SYSTEMS[s["id"]] = system
    says = f"TA98 code {s['ta']}; Latin preferred term \"{pref}\""
    if "TA98 Latin official synonym" in t:
        says += "; Latin official synonym " + ", ".join(f"\"{x}\"" for x in t["TA98 Latin official synonym"])
    says += "; English equivalent " + ", ".join(f"\"{x}\"" for x in t["TA98 English equivalent"])
    if "TA98 English synonym" in t:
        says += "; English synonym " + ", ".join(f"\"{x}\"" for x in t["TA98 English synonym"])
    says += f"; in the hierarchy under {h[2]} \"{system}\""
    evidence.append({"source": "ta98", "locator": f"https://ifaa.unifr.ch/Public/EntryPage/TA98%20Tree/Entity%20TA98%20EN/{s['ta'][1:]}%20Entity%20TA98%20EN.htm", "says": says, "retrieved": R})
    ui = s["mesh"]
    en_h, sv_t = terms[ui]
    ms = f"{ui} \"{en_h}\": Swedish term \"{sv_t}\""
    if syn[ui]:
        ms += "; Swedish synonyms " + ", ".join(f"\"{x}\"" for x in syn[ui])
    evidence.append({"source": "svensk-mesh", "locator": f"https://mesh.kib.ki.se/term/{ui}/", "says": ms, "retrieved": R})
    for kind, key, quote in s["q"]:
        if kind == "msv":
            assert ws(quote) in ws(msv[key]), (s["id"], quote)
            evidence.append({"source": "svensk-mesh", "locator": f"https://mesh.kib.ki.se/term/{key}/ (Swedish scope note, swe_scope_notes.csv of the 2026 download)", "says": f"\"{quote}\"", "retrieved": R})
        elif kind == "men":
            assert ws(quote) in ws(men[key]), (s["id"], quote)
            evidence.append({"source": "svensk-mesh", "locator": f"https://mesh.kib.ki.se/term/{key}/ (NLM English scope note, scope_notes.csv of the 2026 download)", "says": f"\"{quote}\"", "retrieved": R})
        elif kind == "met":
            assert quote in met[key], (s["id"], quote, met[key])
            evidence.append({"source": "svensk-mesh", "locator": f"https://mesh.kib.ki.se/term/{key}/ (NLM English entry terms, entryterms.csv of the 2026 download)", "says": f"English entry term \"{quote}\"", "retrieved": R})
        else:
            lang = "sv" if kind in ("sv", "svf") else "en"
            page = wiki[kind][key]
            assert ws(quote) in ws(page["text"]), (s["id"], kind, key, quote)
            url = f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/wiki/{key.replace(' ', '_')}"
            evidence.append({"source": f"{lang}-wikipedia", "locator": f"{url} (revision {page['rev']})", "says": f"\"{ws(quote)}\"", "retrieved": R})
    # merge consecutive evidence from the same locator
    merged = []
    for e in evidence:
        if merged and merged[-1]["locator"] == e["locator"] and merged[-1]["source"] == e["source"] and e["source"].endswith("wikipedia"):
            merged[-1]["says"] += " … " + e["says"]
        elif merged and merged[-1]["locator"] == e["locator"] and e["says"].startswith("\""):
            merged[-1]["says"] += " … " + e["says"]
        else:
            merged.append(e)
    for l in ("en", "sv", "la"):
        if not matched[l]:
            auto.append((s["id"], l, text[l], [labels(q) for q in items]))
    card = {"id": s["id"], "front": {"en": s["en"], "sv": s["sv"]}, "back": {"la": s["la"]},
            "backNote": {"en": s["note"][0], "sv": s["note"][1]}, "evidence": merged, "checks": checks}
    nchecks += len(checks)
    cards.append(card)
# uniqueness
for side, l in (("front", "en"), ("front", "sv"), ("back", "la")):
    vals = [c[side][l].casefold() for c in cards]
    assert len(vals) == len(set(vals)), (side, l)
json.dump(cards, open(os.path.join(D, "cards.json"), "w"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print(len(cards), "cards,", nchecks, "checks")
for a in auto:
    i, l, t, labs = a
    print("NO MATCH", i, l, repr(t), [(x[0][l], x[1][l]) for x in labs])
print(json.dumps(SYSTEMS, ensure_ascii=False))
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 51 findings: 25 fixed, 2 rejected after checking, 24 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (160 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Source cross-check and Wikidata machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 44 cards, every side

Every card has evidence from Wikidata and Svensk MeSH (content), the TA98 entity page (verification) and the Swedish or English Wikipedia (verification), most from both. 161 Wikidata checks: the TA98 ID (P1323) of 44 items and every en, sv and la label or alias that equals the card's text apart from case. Every Latin back equals the TA98 Latin preferred term apart from capitalisation; the card sides with no matching Wikidata label, and other discrepancies between the sources and conventions chosen, are listed below with how they were resolved. The Latin always follows TA98's preferred term, never a disagreeing Wikidata label.
